title: Word Ladder
statement: You get a start word, an end word and a list of allowed words, all the same length. In one move you may change a single letter, and the new word must be in the list. Return how many words the shortest chain has, counting both the start and the end word. Return 0 if there is no chain. The start word need not be in the list.

example.caption: hit, hot, dot, dog, cog changes one letter each time. That chain has 5 words.

input.label: begin hit, end cog, list below

idea.sentence: Treat words as graph nodes and one-letter changes as edges, then run a breadth-first search. Find neighbours by hiding one letter (h*t) and reading the bucket of words with that pattern.

jargon.plain: Explore all words one move away, then all two moves away, and so on. The first time you reach the end word is the shortest way.
A word with one letter replaced by *. Words that fit the same pattern differ only in that letter.
All words at the same distance from the start.

watch.inputHint: Three arguments: begin word, end word, word list, e.g. "hit", "cog", ["hot","dot","dog","lot","log","cog"]

vars.meaning: number of words in the list

compare.bruteLabel: Compare every word with every other word

rows.name: Compare every pair
rows.note: For every word, scan the whole list for words one letter off.

rows.name: Pattern buckets + BFS
rows.note: Each word makes L patterns and each pattern string costs L to build. The buckets store all those patterns.

fast.takeaway: Hiding a letter turns the question which words are close to me into a map lookup. Each word is queued once, and BFS makes the first hit the shortest.

stages.title: Pattern buckets
stages.note: For every list word and every position, hide that letter and file the word under the pattern.

stages.title: Start the queue
stages.note: Put the start word in the queue with ladder length 1.

stages.title: Take a word
stages.note: Pop the oldest word and read its patterns, one per position.

stages.title: Queue new neighbours
stages.note: Words in those buckets are one letter away. Unseen ones get length + 1 and join the queue.

stages.title: End word found
stages.note: Reaching the end word returns its length. An empty queue means no chain, so return 0.

edges.title: End word missing
edges.why: Neighbours come only from the list, so the end word can never be reached. The search ends with an empty queue.

edges.title: Start not in the list
edges.why: The start word is only patterns to look up. It never needs a bucket entry of its own.

edges.title: One step apart
edges.why: Single-letter words have the one pattern *. The answer counts words, so one change gives length 2, not 1.

edges.title: Dead-end branch
edges.why: hot and dot are reachable, but cog needs a word like dog or log and tog is two letters from dot. Exploring everything ends in 0.

gotchas.text: The answer counts words, not moves. Start the length at 1 for the start word. Off-by-one here is the most common wrong answer.
Mark a word as seen when you queue it, not when you pop it. A word that sits in many buckets would otherwise be queued many times.
groups.get(pattern) can be undefined, because the start word has patterns that no list word shares. Use groups.get(pattern) ?? [] when reading.

Ranging over a missing map key is safe: groups[pattern] gives a nil slice and the loop runs zero times. Slicing the string as w[:i] + "*" + w[i+1:] is fine for lowercase ASCII, but would split a multi-byte rune.

recap.key: Hide one letter at a time to find words one change away. BFS from the start makes the first time you reach the end the shortest.
recap.complexity: Time O(N · L²). Space O(N · L²).
moves: Group every list word under each of its L patterns
Queue the start word with length 1
Pop a word, read each pattern's bucket
Queue unseen words at length + 1, return when the end word appears
